mathematical_obligations: Nonnegative beta is derived at y=1 from 0<=abs(U 1)<=beta; beta<0 is impossible under the global bound.
For a in [0,1], abs(a*U y)=a*abs(U y)<=abs(U y)<=beta*abs(y)=abs(beta*y). Both closed endpoints are allowed.
The two Gaussian exponentials exp(beta*y) and exp(-beta*y) are integrable by Mathlib integrable_exp_mul_gaussianReal, valid also at v=0.

exp(abs(a*U y)) is dominated pointwise by exp(beta*y)+exp(-beta*y), by the sign split on beta*y. Measurability follows from hU and composition. Both exp(a*U y) and exp(-a*U y) are integrable by this common domination, preventing default Bochner-integral semantics from faking the result.

The centered Gaussian is invariant under y->-y by gaussianReal_map_neg, including zero variance. integral_map plus oddness proves equality of the two exponential integrals, with measurability supplied internally.

Both nonlinear and linear cosh functions are integrable by sum and division of the exponential integrability proofs. Averaging the symmetric exponential pair identifies the target expectation with the cosh expectation.
Real.cosh_le_cosh converts the absolute-value comparison into the pointwise cosh inequality. integral_mono is used with both integrability witnesses.
The Gaussian MGF at beta and -beta gives exp(v*beta^2/2) for both terms. The sign and variance normalization are correct; final algebra yields exp(beta^2*v/2).
